served.stem: A monthly utility bill of $125 rises 10%, then falls 25% from that higher amount. What is the bill in dollars, to the nearest cent?
served.bankWhy: Multiply factors: 125 × 1.1 × 0.75 = 103.13. Naïvely adding gives 106.25, which is wrong.

answer.line: Each change acts on the bill as it stands: 125 x 1.10 x 0.75 = 103.125, or $103.13.

steps: Then take 25 percent off the new amount: 137.50 x 0.75 = 103.125.
Round to the cent: $103.13. The fall is bigger than the rise, and it acts on a bigger base, so the bill ends below $125.

choices.note: 125 x 0.75 = 93.75 applies the cut to the starting bill and leaves the 10 percent rise out.
The cut taken off the raised bill.
Netting +10 and -25 into one 15 percent drop treats both as percents of 125. The 25 percent comes off 137.50, so it takes off more.
137.50 is the bill after the 10 percent rise. One step is left: take 25 percent off it.
125 x 1.10 x 1.25 = 171.875 treats the 25 percent fall as a second rise. A fall multiplies by 0.75.

student.lockIt: Successive percents multiply, and each one acts on the amount as it stands then.
